get.summary: Use this to confirm which user (or developer) the calling key acts as.
get.description: Returns identity, plan info, and rate-limit window for the calling key. Branches on key type.

post.summary: Use this when the user wants to create a new online storefront from scratch.
post.description: Creates a storefront from a `StorefrontManifest`. Returns 201 with the full storefront. If the manifest contains more products than the plan allows, returns **207 Multi-Status** with the storefront created (up to plan cap) plus an `errors` array describing the over-cap items.

207.description: Partial success — see `errors[]` in the body

get.summary: Use this when the user wants to discover storefronts on their Marea account.
get.description: Returns the bearer user's storefronts ordered by storefront id, paginated. `published` is omitted from list items — call GET /v1/storefronts/{storefrontId} for the live publish status; `_links.publicUrl` is returned here. Pass the opaque `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; `nextCursor` is null on the last page.

schema.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response's `nextCursor`. Cursors minted before 2026-09 (raw ISO timestamps) are ignored and the page restarts from the beginning.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response's `nextCursor`. Cursors minted before 2026-09 (raw ISO timestamps) are ignored and the page restarts from the beginning.
parameters.name: cursor

patch.summary: Use this when the user wants to change ANY field of an existing storefront.
patch.description: Partial PATCH (mutability rule §6.18.1.1). Deep-merge for nested objects, full-replace for arrays.

get.summary: Use this when the user wants the full configuration of a single storefront.
get.description: Returns the storefront DTO including the live `published` flag and `_links`. 404 on unknown id or cross-tenant.

post.summary: Use this when the user is ready to take their storefront live.
post.description: Publishes the current state of the storefront. Returns 402 if the plan does not permit publishing, 422 if the storefront has 0 products, 451 if ToS not accepted (PRD-7 hook). Idempotent on republish.

post.summary: Use this when the user wants to add a product to an existing storefront.

get.summary: Use this when the user wants to list products in a storefront's catalog.
get.description: Returns products under the storefront ordered by product id, paginated. Hidden products (`hide:true`) are excluded by default — pass `includeHidden=true` to see them. Pass the opaque `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; `nextCursor` is null on the last page.

schema.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response's `nextCursor`. Cursors minted before 2026-09 (raw ISO timestamps) are ignored and the page restarts from the beginning.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response's `nextCursor`. Cursors minted before 2026-09 (raw ISO timestamps) are ignored and the page restarts from the beginning.
parameters.name: cursor

schema.description: Include products with `hide: true`. Accepts `true`, `1` or `yes`.

parameters.description: Include products with `hide: true`. Accepts `true`, `1` or `yes`.
parameters.name: includeHidden

patch.summary: Use this when the user wants to change ANY field of an existing product.

post.summary: Use this when an agent wants to create a Marea account on behalf of a user with one round-trip (account + storefront + verification email).
post.description: Creates a Firebase Auth user + Firestore user doc + restricted user key + (optionally) a starter storefront via createMenuCore + sends a 6-digit verification email. Returns 201, or 207 when the account was created but the storefront was not fully applied (plan-cap overflow, or the storefront could not be created at all — see errors[]). The account and userKey are returned either way; the userKey is returned ONCE — store it.

207.description: Partial success — see `errors[]` in the body

get.summary: Use this to list every user this developer key has bootstrapped (paginated 50/page).
get.description: Returns users where createdByDeveloper.keyId === ctx.keyId, ordered by createdAt DESC. Use the returned `nextCursor` (createdAt ISO string) for the next page.

post.summary: Use this when the user has read back the 6-digit code from their email and you want to upgrade the user-key to full scope.
post.description: Validates the 6-digit code (3 attempts max), upgrades the bootstrap user-key from restricted to full scope (same key — no rotation), flips agentBootstrapped→false + verificationStatus→verified, fires the user.verified webhook stub. Cross-tenant/wrong-id → 404 leak-less.

post.summary: Use this when the verification email may have been lost or the code expired and you want to issue a fresh code without re-bootstrapping.
post.description: Per-user rate-limited (3/hour, 5/day). Overwrites the existing apiVerificationCodes/{email} doc — old code is voided automatically. Returns the new expiry timestamp.

get.summary: Use this to poll the status of a user you previously bootstrapped (verificationStatus, plan, recent events).
get.description: Returns the user DTO. Cross-developer isolation: only users that THIS developer key bootstrapped are visible — wrong-id or other-developer's-user → 404 leak-less per RFC §10.4.

post.summary: Use this to issue an additional restricted user key for a verified user you previously bootstrapped (e.g. a second integration).
post.description: Validates that the user was bootstrapped by THIS developer and is verified (verificationStatus==="verified"). Returns the raw user key once. Cross-developer attempt → 404 leak-less; pre-verify call → 422.

post.summary: Use this when you want to register a webhook endpoint that receives one or more event types (`user.verified`, `user.cancelled`, `order.*`).
post.description: Creates a webhook endpoint as a first-class object. The returned `signingSecret` is the only time the secret is visible — store it now; rotate via `POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}/rotate-secret` if lost. Per-event subscription is controlled by `subscribedEvents`. A developer endpoint can subscribe to `order.*` events from any storefront the caller bootstrapped — Marea resolves the merchant → developer chain at dispatch time, so one endpoint covers every storefront. Hard caps: 16 endpoints per account; URL ≤2048 chars; HTTPS only; rejects loopback / private / metadata hostnames.

get.summary: Use this when you want to list every webhook endpoint owned by the caller (developer scope).
get.description: Returns up to 16 endpoints (cap per account). Never returns the signing secret — use `POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}/rotate-secret` if you need a new one.

get.summary: Use this when you want to fetch a single webhook endpoint by its id.
get.description: Returns the endpoint excluding the signing secret. Useful for verifying current event subscriptions, enablement status, and recent-delivery summary.

post.summary: Use this when you want to patch one or more fields of an existing webhook endpoint (url, description, enabled, subscribedEvents).
post.description: Accepts a partial update; only the fields present in the body are modified. Cannot rotate the signing secret here — use the dedicated rotate-secret callable / endpoint. Does NOT return the signing secret.

delete.summary: Use this when you want to permanently delete a webhook endpoint. To stop dispatch without losing the URL, use `enabled: false` via the update endpoint instead.
delete.description: Hard delete — there is no soft-delete state for endpoints. Idempotent for 404 callers (returns 404 if already absent).

post.summary: Use this when you want to rotate the signing secret of a webhook endpoint. Returns the new secret ONCE; the old secret stops working immediately.
post.description: No overlap window in v1 — coordinate the rotation with your receiver. The returned `signingSecret` is the only time the new secret is visible; store it before responding to the next webhook. Bumps `signingSecretVersion` by one.

ApiNextAction.description: A concrete action the agent can offer the user.

previewUrl.description: Optional preview link the agent can surface.

type.description: High-level error category. Agents branch on this.

doc.description: Link to the error reference in the docs.

ApiErrorResponse.description: §9.6 uniform error envelope. Every non-2xx response uses this shape.

tier.description: Plan tier the calling user is on. Numeric internal plans map to one of these 4.

MeResponse.description: Identity + plan info for the calling key. Available to both user and developer keys (branched by `type`).

ProductManifest.description: Agent-facing product input shape. Mutability rule §6.18.1.1: every field PATCHable post-create.

blocks.description: REPLACES the whole block list. On PATCH, send the complete array — anything you omit is removed, not merged.

categories.description: REPLACES the whole category list. On PATCH, send the complete array — categories you omit are deleted, and products still referencing them keep an orphan category string.

StorefrontManifest.description: Agent-facing storefront input shape (RFC §6.18.1). Every field is PATCHable per §6.18.1.1.

blocks.description: REPLACES the whole block list. On PATCH, send the complete array — anything you omit is removed, not merged.

categories.description: REPLACES the whole category list. On PATCH, send the complete array — categories you omit are deleted, and products still referencing them keep an orphan category string.

StorefrontManifestPatch.description: PATCH body. Omitted fields are untouched; array fields (`categories`, `blocks`) REPLACE the stored list, so send the complete array. `products[]` is rejected — use POST /v1/storefronts/{storefrontId}/products. `whatsapp` is rejected on PATCH: the order number can only be set at creation or changed in the dashboard.

ProductManifestPatch.description: PATCH body. Omitted fields are untouched. Sending `salePrice` alone is checked against the stored `price`.

ApiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyHeader.description: Alternative to `Authorization: Bearer`. Same `mk_*` value. Use only when your environment cannot send the `Authorization` header.
